starter.text:
import random
from micrograd.nn import MLP

random.seed(0)
X = [[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1]]
Y = [-1, 1, 1, -1]
model = MLP(2, [8, 1])
for step in range(300):
    preds = [model(x) for x in X]
    loss = sum((p - y) ** 2 for p, y in zip(preds, Y))
    model.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    for p in model.parameters():
        p.data -= 0.05 * p.grad
print(f"loss {loss.data:.4f}", [round(p.data, 2) for p in preds])

verify.expect: loss 0.0000 [-1.0, 1.0, 1.0, -1.0] with zero_grad. Without it: loss 4.0000 [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], because gradients from every earlier step pile up.

starter.text:
import math
import sys

import gymnasium as gym
import numpy as np

ANGLE_LIMIT = 12 * 2 * math.pi / 360  # cartpole.py line 136
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def random_policy(obs):
    return int(rng.integers(2))


def angle_policy(obs):
    return 0  # TODO: push toward the side the pole leans to


def lean_policy(obs):
    return 0  # TODO: also use the angular velocity, obs[3]


def play(policy, seed):
    env = gym.make("CartPole-v1")
    obs, _ = env.reset(seed=seed)
    total = 0.0
    while True:
        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, _ = env.step(policy(obs))
        total += reward
        if terminated or truncated:
            return total, terminated, truncated, obs


name = sys.argv[1]
policy = {"random": random_policy, "angle": angle_policy, "lean": lean_policy}[name]
runs = [play(policy, seed) for seed in range(20)]
mean = sum(r[0] for r in runs) / len(runs)
terminated = sum(r[1] for r in runs)
truncated = sum(r[2] for r in runs)
print(f"{name}: mean {mean:.1f}  terminated {terminated}/20  truncated {truncated}/20")

tasks.do: The observation is [cart position, cart velocity, pole angle, pole angular velocity] (lines 44 to 51). A positive angle means the pole leans toward +x, and pushing the cart right (action 1) swings it back. Pushing toward the lean reacts only after the pole has moved; adding the angular velocity also counts where the pole is heading.

tasks.title: Tell termination from truncation
tasks.do: CartPole-v1 is registered with max_episode_steps=500 (line 30). gym.make then wraps the environment in TimeLimit (gymnasium/envs/registration.py lines 812 to 816), and TimeLimit.step sets truncated=True once 500 steps have run (gymnasium/wrappers/common.py lines 130 to 136). terminated means the task ended: the pole fell and no more reward can come. truncated means the run was cut off while the pole was still up, so a learning agent should still count the reward it would have earned (bootstrap). tasks.title: Replace the hand update with torch.optim.SGD
tasks.do: Lines 59 and 60 apply gradient descent by hand: each parameter moves by -0.1 times its gradient, after line 49 has cleared the old gradients. torch.optim.SGD(params, lr=0.1) does the same in optimizer.step() and optimizer.zero_grad(). The arithmetic differs slightly: line 60 rounds -0.1 * grad to float32 before adding it, and SGD adds the gradient with alpha=-0.1 in one operation. tasks.title: Split one document into linked chunks
tasks.do: get_nodes_from_documents splits each Document with SentenceSplitter and turns each chunk into a TextNode. _postprocess_parsed_nodes then finds each chunk in the source text with str.find to set start_char_idx and end_char_idx (lines 104 to 118). It adds PREVIOUS and NEXT relationships only when two neighbouring nodes come from the same document (lines 134 to 153). ref_doc_id reads the SOURCE relationship. chunk_size and chunk_overlap count cl100k_base tokens, not words; each sentence here is about 12 tokens.

starter.text:
from llama_index.core import Document
from llama_index.core.node_parser import SentenceSplitter

TOPICS = ["cache", "queue", "index", "token", "shard"]
sentences = [f"Sentence {i} explains the {TOPICS[i % 5]} in one short line." for i in range(40)]
docs = [Document(text=" ".join(sentences), id_="doc-1")]

splitter = SentenceSplitter(chunk_size=64, chunk_overlap=16)
nodes = splitter.get_nodes_from_documents(docs)
print("nodes", len(nodes))
for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
    links = ("prev" if node.prev_node else "-") + " " + ("next" if node.next_node else "-")
    first = node.text.split()[1]
    print(i, node.ref_doc_id, f"chars {node.start_char_idx}-{node.end_char_idx}", links, "first sentence", first)

tasks.do: SimpleKeywordTableIndex maps each keyword to the nodes that contain it. simple_extract_keywords (keyword_table/utils.py lines 11 to 21) lowercases the words and drops NLTK's English stopwords. starter.text:
from llama_index.core import Document, Settings, SimpleKeywordTableIndex
from llama_index.core.llms import MockLLM
from llama_index.core.node_parser import SentenceSplitter

Settings.llm = MockLLM()  # no hosted model; the keyword index never calls it

NOTES = {
    "cache": "A cache keeps recent results in memory so repeated reads skip the database.",
    "queue": "A queue holds jobs until a worker is free to process them in order.",
    "shard": "Sharding splits one large table across several servers by key.",
    "index": "A database index sorts one column so lookups avoid a full table scan.",
    "retry": "Retries with exponential backoff wait longer after each failed request.",
    "token": "A tokenizer cuts text into tokens before a model can read it.",
    "replica": "A replica copies the primary database so reads survive a server failure.",
    "chunk": "Chunking cuts long documents into overlapping pieces before indexing.",
}
QUERIES = [
    ("why do repeated reads skip the database", "cache"),
    ("which worker takes the jobs", "queue"),
    ("put a table across servers", "shard"),
    ("how long to wait after a failed request", "retry"),
    ("turn text into tokens", "token"),
    ("keep reads alive when a server fails", "replica"),
]

docs = [Document(text=text, id_=doc_id) for doc_id, text in NOTES.items()]
nodes = SentenceSplitter(chunk_size=64, chunk_overlap=16).get_nodes_from_documents(docs)
retriever = SimpleKeywordTableIndex(nodes).as_retriever(num_chunks_per_query=3)


def recall_at_k(k):
    """Share of queries whose source note is among the first k results."""
    hits = 0
    for query, doc_id in QUERIES:
        results = retriever.retrieve(query)
        # TODO: add 1 to hits when doc_id is the ref_doc_id of one of the first k results
    return hits / len(QUERIES)


for k in (1, 3):
    print(f"recall@{k} {recall_at_k(k):.2f} over {len(QUERIES)} queries")

verify.expect: recall@1 1.00 and recall@3 1.00 over 6 queries. With the new queries: recall@1 0.75 over 8 queries and recall@3 0.88 over 8 queries. The first new query shares no word with the index note, so nothing comes back. The second matches two words of the cache note and one of the replica note, so the right note comes second.

tasks.do: A cursor names the last row the client has seen, and the next page starts strictly after it, so rows inserted above it do not move it. import gymnasium as gym
from stable_baselines3 import PPO
from stable_baselines3.common.evaluation import evaluate_policy
from stable_baselines3.common.monitor import Monitor


def eval_env(seed):
    env = Monitor(gym.make("CartPole-v1"))
    env.reset(seed=seed)
    env.action_space.seed(seed)
    return env


def random_baseline(env, episodes=20):
    totals = []
    for _ in range(episodes):
        env.reset()
        total, done = 0.0, False
        while not done:
            _, reward, terminated, truncated, _ = env.step(env.action_space.sample())
            total += reward
            done = terminated or truncated
        totals.append(total)
    return sum(totals) / len(totals)


model = PPO("MlpPolicy", gym.make("CartPole-v1"), seed=0, device="cpu")
model.learn(total_timesteps=50_000)
mean, std = evaluate_policy(model, eval_env(123), n_eval_episodes=20, deterministic=True)
print(f"random {random_baseline(eval_env(123)):.1f}  ppo {mean:.1f} +/- {std:.1f}")
print("PASS" if mean >= 475 else "TRAIN LONGER")

import gymnasium as gym
from corridor import Corridor
from stable_baselines3 import PPO
from stable_baselines3.common.evaluation import evaluate_policy
from stable_baselines3.common.monitor import Monitor


class CoinCorridor(Corridor):
    def step(self, action):
        obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = super().step(action)
        if self.pos == 5:
            reward += 0.2
        return obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info


env = gym.wrappers.TimeLimit(CoinCorridor(), max_episode_steps=50)
model = PPO("MlpPolicy", env, seed=0, device="cpu")
model.learn(total_timesteps=20_000)
rewards, lengths = evaluate_policy(model, Monitor(gym.wrappers.TimeLimit(CoinCorridor(), 50)),
                                   n_eval_episodes=10, deterministic=True, return_episode_rewards=True)
reached = sum(length < 50 for length in lengths)
print(f"mean reward {sum(rewards) / len(rewards):.2f}  reached goal {reached}/10")
